title: Longest even record
prompt:
A team's season is a string of match results, "W" for a win and "L" for a loss. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive matches with exactly as many wins as losses. Return 0 if there is none.

- results has 0 to 100,000 characters, each "W" or "L".
- Return an integer.
hints: Score a win as +1 and a loss as -1. A run is even exactly when its score adds up to 0.
Keep a running score. A run from just after i up to j is even when score[j] equals score[i].
Store the first index where each running score appears, starting with score 0 at index -1. At each match, if this score was seen before, the run since then is even; keep the longest.

solution.explanation: The running balance is a prefix sum of +1 and -1. Two equal balances mean the matches between them cancel out. Keeping only the first index of each balance makes every run as long as possible, and seeding balance 0 at index -1 covers runs that start at the first match.

complexity.notes: One pass with expected O(1) map operations. The map holds at most n + 1 balances.

followUps: Count how many even runs there are instead of the longest one.
Draws ("D") are added and count as neither. How does the balance change?
